key_points: By the 9th century, south India saw the rise of assemblies at several levels.
A simplified map of a few dynasties in north and peninsular India from the 7th century onward.
Your first stop is Kannauj, a city by River Ganga where a powerful king hosts poets and scholars.
As Chola dominance in south India lasted until the 13th century, we will meet them again in the next chapter.
The Rāṣhṭrakūṭa king Krishna I got the magnificent Kailaśhanātha temple, the largest rock-cut temple in India (Fig.
A few of the more powerful kingdoms rose to the status of empires, but rarely managed to cover a large part of India or to last more than a couple of centuries.
The Pallavas ruled over much of northern Tamil Nadu and southern Andhra Pradesh until the late 9th century, when they were finally overthrown by the Chola king Aditya I.
The geographer al-Istakhri observed that after three centuries of unremitting effort, the Arab dominion in India was limited to just two petty states in Sindh and Punjab.
Still, there is no doubt that in the early 7 th century the most of India was dominated by two great imperial powers — Harṣhavardhana north of the Vindhyas and Pulakeśhin II south of them.
Now, two centuries later, Xuanzang (his name was earlier transcribed as Hsuan Tsang or Hiuen Tsang) set out on his journey to India and travelled around the subcontinent between 630 and 644.
